question: Which exact firmware functions are the stock message box constructor and content setter and the object delete of this Band 11 build? The earlier ensemble candidates (0xc43e7d0 a font metrics routine, 0xc566b9c the alarm clock back handler, 0xc720e98 memset) were not them.
callsite_evidence: The strings page_msgbox, lvx_page_msgbox_destructor, add_event_to_page and the lvx_page_msgbox.c path lead to sub_C508070 (add_event_to_page) and sub_C508104 (destructor); the destructor is the class destructor of the class table at 0x2ca3eba8-0x2ca3ebb8, whose only constructor users are sub_C50FD30 (msgbox object creation with the 0x74-byte instance setup) and the one-line wrappers sub_C50FDB0 / sub_C50FDBC.
Stock alarmclock pages call sub_C50FDBC(parent, 0) then sub_C50EDD4(box, 5, ...) to build their message boxes (render_reconnect_view, jump reminder).

sub_C50EDD4 has the same structure as the Band 10 Pro 3.101.043 set_content sub_C4CA130 (mode 5 icon pair cancel.bin/confirm.bin, mode switch, text/button helpers), with the button record widened to 28 bytes.
sub_C380404 is called by lv_obj_clean (sub_C384DB4) for each child and sets the deleting flag, sends event 36 and frees the object: lv_obj_delete.
The same bytes sit at the same addresses in 4.100.139 and 4.100.155.
ownership_analysis: The message box is a page-owned object; the host deletes it from its own button callback, as the stock Band 10 Pro callers do.
unsafe_assumptions: Static recovery only; the Mirage run is emulator evidence, not device verification.
recommended_probe: Open a module dialog on Mirage 4.100.155 and compare it with the stock alarm message box.
